description: Serve a saved Model over HTTP for synchronous and batch prediction, promote and roll back versions without rebuilding an image, and trigger retraining as a job. Begins where MODEL-FLOW ends: at a committed Model row. This ledger owns nothing before Save Model.
progress_note: Written 2026-08-24 from the MODEL-FLOW ledger alone, NOT from a code read. Every finding below is marked UNVERIFIED unless stated otherwise, and MODEL-SERVE-000 exists to replace them with facts before anything is built. Precedent for taking that seriously: MODEL-FLOW-000's own re-audit found five of its seven tasks describing code that was already correct, and one task (T03) whose premise was inverted against the tree.
upstream: MODEL-FLOW ledger — this one assumes MODEL-FLOW-007 (Save Model) has landed. It has NOT: MODEL-FLOW-007 is pending, behind -004 (pending), -005 (blocked) and -006 (pending). Nothing here can be verified end to end until a Model row can be created by the wizard at all.

training_and_serving_are_separate_planes.rationale: Training is a job that exits; serving is a process that must stay up. They differ in resource shape (a fit spikes memory, an inference does not), in scaling (train scales to zero, serving needs a warm replica), and in failure handling (a job retries, a service must stay available). Running a fit inside the serving process couples them at the worst point: the fit's memory spike is charged to the same cgroup as the live model cache, so a retrain can OOM-kill the endpoint that is currently answering. The trainer image also carries fit-time dependencies a serving process never calls, which is dead weight on every cold start.
training_and_serving_are_separate_planes.consequence: POST /retrain never fits anything itself. It records intent and returns; the existing trainer image does the work, spawned the same way MODEL-FLOW-003-T04 already spawns it.
training_and_serving_are_separate_planes.scope_correction: NARROWED 2026-08-25. This decision remains right for a long-running synchronous serving process (MODEL-SERVE-002) and for never fitting inside one. It was over-applied when written: it was read as 'inference always needs its own image', and scheduled batch inference is a counterexample its own rationale does not cover. See short_lived_containers_for_scheduled_inference. MODEL-SERVE-002-T01 (a separate serving image) is unaffected and stays.

deploy_is_a_row_change_not_an_image_buil.chosen: One generic serving image; the production pointer lives in Postgres
deploy_is_a_row_change_not_an_image_buil.rationale: The alternative — one image per model — makes every retrain a CI run and every rollback a redeploy, and turns N models into N deployments to operate. Since the model is data the process loads, not code it links against, the version in production is a fact about a row. Promotion becomes an UPDATE and rollback becomes the same UPDATE in reverse, which is what makes rollback fast enough to actually use during an incident.

rejected.One container per model: Isolates dependencies perfectly and keeps the blast radius to one model, which is the right call ONLY if models genuinely disagree about their dependencies. Revisit per FRAMEWORK, not per model: if MODEL-FLOW-009 lands and brings torch or tensorflow into the picture, a second serving image for sequence models is justified where a second image per tabular model is not.
rejected.A mutable latest/ key in MinIO: Rejected for the reason MODEL-FLOW-007-T10 already gives on the training side: overwriting an object destroys the thing you roll back TO. It also cannot be read consistently — two replicas can observe different bytes behind one key with no way to tell.

retrain_is_blocked_on_the_same_definitio.note: See MODEL-FLOW decisions.fine_tuning_undefined and retrain_and_fine_tuning_are_one_question. MODEL-SERVE-004 is blocked on that decision, not on engineering. Recording it as its own blocked feature rather than as work is deliberate: sizing it as buildable would understate it exactly the way sizing lstm/gru as a build_model branch would have (MODEL-FLOW-009's own blocked_on says so).

serving_host_undecided.note:
Training today spawns containers against a Docker daemon and tracks them with an in-memory watch() (trainning-container.authorized.service.ts). That mechanism is known-unsuitable for a long-running service — MODEL-FLOW-003-V01 observed a run stranded at RUNNING forever because a nest --watch restart killed the tracker, and MODEL-FLOW-011-T04 was opened to reconcile it. A serving process outliving the Node process that spawned it is the NORMAL case, not the exception, so the same design would be permanently wrong rather than occasionally.

OPTIONS, not yet chosen: (a) keep the Docker-daemon spawn and give serving its own supervisor with boot reconciliation; (b) run serving as an ordinary long-lived service in the same compose/orchestrator as the backend, spawned by nothing; (c) an external orchestrator. (b) is the smallest and is the default unless someone needs per-model isolation. DECIDE BEFORE MODEL-SERVE-002 — the answer changes what that feature builds, not just where it runs.

short_lived_containers_for_scheduled_inf.chosen: Short-lived containers on the existing trainer image, second entrypoint
short_lived_containers_for_scheduled_inf.rationale: REVISES the scope of training_and_serving_are_separate_planes rather than contradicting it. That decision's reason is specific: a FIT spikes memory and, sharing a cgroup with a long-running cache, can OOM-kill the endpoint currently answering. Hourly batch inference is not a long-running process and holds no cache, so that reason does not apply to it. What is left is a comparison the existing code wins outright — trainning-container.authorized.service.ts already spawns, resource-limits and reaps containers; ModelTrainingRunLog and the /log callback already give per-run logs; image_digest provenance already comes for free. A second entrypoint (infer.py) beside train.py in images/trainer/ reuses all of it. Cold start is a python import, 3-5s, which is noise at a one-hour cadence.
short_lived_containers_for_scheduled_inf.consequence: MODEL-SERVE-006 needs no serving process, no cache-invalidation-on-promote, and no readiness protocol. Those belong to MODEL-SERVE-002 (synchronous /predict) alone, which is a SEPARATE requirement arriving later — do not build a serving service in order to get an hourly run.
short_lived_containers_for_scheduled_inf.also: One image, not two, additionally removes a divergence risk the two-image plan created: both entrypoints unpickle the same model.joblib, so they cannot disagree about the library that wrote it.

metrics_are_derived_from_predictions_not.chosen: predictions.parquet is the source of truth; metrics.json is a cache
metrics_are_derived_from_predictions_not.rationale: The alternative — the client sends a metric set and the container computes exactly those — has one failure that gets worse over time: adding a metric next month leaves every existing run without it, so a comparison table shows a column of em-dashes, and the only way to fill it is to RETRAIN models in order to compute a number that never needed a fit. Deriving from the stored predictions instead means a new metric is recomputable across all history, and the same definitions serve both evaluation (test-split predictions) and monitoring (inference predictions) — one implementation, so 'r2 at training' and 'r2 in monitoring' cannot drift into two numbers that look comparable and are not.
metrics_are_derived_from_predictions_not.constraint: STATE THE BOUNDARY EXPLICITLY IN THE REGISTRY. Only metrics computable from (actual, predicted) plus scalars already in run_manifest.json (e.g. feature_count for adjusted R²) are backfillable. Anything needing feature values, residual-vs-feature structure or model internals is NOT, and must be marked so — otherwise the registry mixes metrics that can be added retroactively with metrics that cannot, in one table, and nobody can tell which is which.

deploy_status_currently_asserts_somethin.note:
OBSERVED 2026-08-25 in phase-4-deploy.tsx. Save & Deploy performs `updateModel(modelId, { deployStatus: 'running' })` and nothing else: no container, no schedule, no inference. The component is internally honest — its own comment explains why deploy is a second write and why the retrain/drift atoms are deliberately NOT rendered ('nothing persists them, so rendering them would collect settings that go nowhere'), which is the correct call and anticipated this ledger. The problem is the WORD: anyone reading the models list sees 'running' and concludes predictions are being produced.

This is therefore not a new feature to add but an existing claim to make true, which changes MODEL-SERVE-006's framing: deployStatus must become DERIVED from the last successful InferenceWindow, not a column any caller can set. Two writable sources of truth for 'is this deployed' is the same class of problem as a mutable latest/ key, rejected above for the same reason.

The atoms the comment names (mpAutoRetrainAtom and the drift/SD siblings) are the config a scheduler needs. They already exist client-side and are unpersisted — MODEL-SERVE-006-T09 is where they acquire a home.

findings: CORRECTED 2026-08-24 FROM A MINIO SCREENSHOT OF A REAL RUN (bucket `datasets`, key drafts/1ce30923-394b-4135-b324-0e913606dcf9/runs/61f9aa28-0c31-4e99-bd52-4674200f72f6/, timestamps 2026-08-19 11:44 — one of the two runs MODEL-FLOW-003-V01 live-verified). The prior finding called the run's descriptor `manifest.json`; the object is `run_manifest.json`. The rename is not cosmetic: the name scopes it to the RUN, and a run descriptor and a serving descriptor are not the same document. A run manifest records what happened during a fit; serving needs what is required to LOAD the result. They may overlap, but assuming they are identical is exactly the kind of assumption MODEL-SERVE-000 exists to stop. Contents remain UNVERIFIED — the screenshot shows names and sizes only.

NEW AND HIGHEST SEVERITY IN THIS LEDGER — THE RUN DIRECTORY IS NOT A SELF-CONTAINED SERVING BUNDLE, CONFIRMED BY OBSERVATION. The directory holds exactly four objects: metrics.json (155 B), model.joblib (1.1 KiB), predictions.parquet (24.9 KiB), run_manifest.json (1.2 KiB). There is NO feature_spec.json and NO scaler or preprocessor object. model.joblib at 1.1 KiB is corroborating evidence rather than proof, but it is strong: a fitted sklearn Pipeline carrying a scaler's own state does not serialise to a kilobyte — this is an estimator alone.

So a serving process cannot open this prefix and predict. It must resolve Model -> ModelTrainingRun -> DatasetArtifact.featureSpecKey -> feature_spec.json, three hops across two entities, and the transform state (scalers, the effective column list from select_columns + force_keep_target) lives at the far end of that chain on an entity the USER CAN EDIT.

This upgrades, not merely confirms, the train/serve skew finding. The prior finding treated skew as a risk of REIMPLEMENTING the transform. The real exposure is that the transform's inputs are not co-located with the model at all, so a correct implementation can still be fed the wrong spec — a failure that produces a plausible number, which is the MODEL-FLOW-000-T02 shape again.

NEW — NOTHING PINS OR PROTECTS THE ARTIFACT A MODEL WAS FITTED AGAINST. MODEL-FLOW-010's own finding states that editing a dataset keeps the Dataset id and moves currentArtifactId, and correctly concludes that ModelDraft.datasetId stays valid. That conclusion is right for the WIZARD and wrong to inherit here: a served model needs the SPECIFIC artifact it was fitted against, not the dataset's current one, and neither ledger says that artifact is retained for as long as a model references it. Two separate objects can therefore be reclaimed out from under one production model — its bytes (guarded upstream by MODEL-FLOW-011-T05) and its feature spec (guarded by nothing). Losing either is the same outage.

NEW — ONE BUCKET HOLDS EVERYTHING. Model run outputs live in the `datasets` bucket (17.4 MiB / 138 objects at the time of the screenshot). That is fine today and cheap to leave alone, but it means no bucket-scoped lifecycle rule, retention policy or access grant can distinguish a production model's bytes from an abandoned dataset draft's. Anyone who later writes a lifecycle rule intending it for datasets writes it for models too. Record it now so that decision is made deliberately rather than discovered.

NEW AND USEFUL — MODEL-SERVE-002-V01 IS RUNNABLE TODAY. predictions.parquet exists in the run directory (24.9 KiB), so the no-skew test — score a row from the model's own test split through the live endpoint and assert it matches the recorded prediction — has real reference data against a real fitted model, with no live wizard and no MODEL-FLOW-007 required. This is the one verification in this ledger that can be built before its own dependencies land, and it is also the most load-bearing.

NEW — NO CHECKSUM SIDECAR EXISTS. There is no .sha256 or equivalent object beside model.joblib, so a checksum either lives inside run_manifest.json or is not computed at all. MODEL-SERVE-000-T01 must distinguish those two, because they lead to different work: reading a field, versus adding a write to the trainer AND accepting that every artifact predating that change has no checksum and needs a stated policy.

CONFIRMED 2026-08-24 by reading run_manifest.json from the run in the screenshot. The prior finding, and MODEL-SERVE-000-T01's three questions, are now answered and the finding is REPLACED rather than deleted so the audit trail survives: (1) a checksum EXISTS — model_sha256, plus artifact_checksum for the GOLD parquet; (2) provenance is pinned by image_digest (scgc/soft-sensor-trainer@sha256:…), which is STRONGER than the sklearn/joblib version string this ledger asked for, because it pins the whole runtime rather than one library; (3) the manifest does NOT carry a featureSpecKey, but it DOES inline feature_columns, target_y, target_scaled and derived_from_target — four of the fields serving would otherwise have walked to the spec for. seed and the full split record (method, ratio, cut_timestamp, labelled/train/test rows) are also present. This manifest is materially better than this ledger assumed, and the earlier UNVERIFIED framing overstated the gap.

NARROWED 2026-08-24 — THE ONLY MISSING SERVING INPUT IS SCALER STATE. With feature_columns inlined, the three-hop chain to feature_spec.json collapses to one open question rather than a general dependency: where does a run's SCALER configuration live, and is it recoverable at serve time? The manifest records target_scaled: false, which proves the system tracks scaling on the target side, and records nothing about the feature side. model.joblib at 1.1 KiB for a bare 8-feature OLS is consistent with this particular run having no scalers at all — which is why it cannot answer the question. MODEL-SERVE-000-T03 must therefore be run against a run that DID scale, not this one; the smallest, cleanest artifact is the least informative one here.

IMAGE_DIGEST CREATES A NEW RETENTION DEPENDENCY. Pinning by digest is the right call, but a digest pins nothing once the image is garbage-collected from the registry — at which point the ONLY record of the runtime a production model was fitted under is a string that resolves to nothing. Whatever retains the model object and its artifact must extend to the trainer image any live ModelVersion names. This dependency did not exist under the version-string approach this ledger originally proposed; it is a consequence of the better mechanism, not a defect in it.

NEW — `drafts/` IS A SHARED ROOT FOR TWO UNRELATED ENTITIES IN ONE BUCKET. Observed directly: the run lives at drafts/1ce30923-…/runs/… (a ModelDraft) while its gold_object_key reads drafts/c47bfa69-…/artifacts/… (a DatasetDraft). Same bucket, same first segment, different tables, different lifecycles, different sweepers. UUIDs will not collide, so this is not a correctness bug today. The exposure is in the SWEEPERS: MODEL-FLOW-011-T02 already specifies is_draft_run_key rather than a string prefix match, which is correct — but DS-LAKE-014's DatasetDraft sweeper predates that guidance and it is UNVERIFIED whether it reclaims by structural predicate or by a drafts/{id}/ prefix. If the latter, a dataset sweep can reach a model draft's prefix. Hand to MODEL-SERVE-000-T06's read; the fix, if needed, is upstream.

NEW — NOTHING GATES PROMOTION ON WHETHER THE MODEL IS ANY GOOD. The observed run has r2 = -2.4068: worse than predicting the mean, i.e. no predictive value. Every claim made about it is nonetheless true — MODEL-FLOW-003-V01 correctly recorded it as SUCCEEDED with real metrics, and the leakage guard correctly found nothing to check (derived_from_target is empty, so there is no leakage; the model is simply bad). MODEL-FLOW-000-T02 hardened this codebase against an implausibly HIGH R², and this is the opposite direction, which no criterion in either ledger covers. MODEL-SERVE-001-T05 refuses a version whose artifact cannot be LOADED; it says nothing about one that loads fine and is useless. See MODEL-SERVE-001-T06.

NEW 2026-08-25, READ FROM SOURCE — STEP 4 EVALUATION DOES NOT DISPLAY THE CONTAINER'S METRICS AT ALL. phase-3-evaluation.tsx computes every figure client-side: it picks `const xTag = modelReady.tags.find(t => t !== target)` — the first tag that is not the target — and runs computeFit(modelReady, xTag, target), a single-feature fit in the browser. The 8-feature fit the container actually performed is never read; mpTrainingResultAtom is not imported by this file. The compared-model series is explicitly mock (seededNoise + a comment saying real per-model predictions arrive later). mpSelectedMetricsAtom is a DISPLAY FILTER over these locally-computed values.

CONSEQUENCE, AND IT EXPLAINS AN EARLIER FINDING: r2 = -2.4068 is invisible in the product. The screen shows a plausible chart from a different fit, which is why a model with no predictive value passed through the wizard without anyone stumbling. The MODEL-FLOW ledger is not wrong about this — MODEL-FLOW-003-V02 claims metrics are 'available', not consumed, and says so in as many words, and every MODEL-FLOW-004 task is still pending. The gap is real, correctly recorded upstream, and it is a HARD PREREQUISITE for anything in this ledger that touches metrics: a metric registry wired to a screen that computes its own numbers changes which locally-computed values are shown and nothing else.

NEW 2026-08-25 — 'CHANGE THE EVALUATION METRICS FROM THE UI' IS NOT REACHABLE FROM WHERE THE UI IS TODAY. The request is well-formed and the design answer is in decisions.metrics_are_derived_from_predictions_not_computed_at_fit, but ordering matters: mpSelectedMetricsAtom currently filters browser-computed values, so pointing it at a registry while phase-3-evaluation.tsx still calls computeFit produces a prettier filter over the wrong numbers. MODEL-FLOW-004 first, registry second. Recorded as a sequencing constraint rather than a defect.

NEW 2026-08-25 — THE WIZARD'S OWN GATE IS LOOSER THAN THE RUN-CREATION GUARD BEHIND IT. phase-2-training-config.tsx computes `canTrain = targetVariables.length > 0 && training.status !== 'training' && tags.length > 0`, and renders AutoMlToggles as freely operable. MODEL-FLOW-003-T10 established that use-model-training refuses anything other than exactly one target, exactly one algorithm, and AutoML off. So the button is enabled for states the layer beneath it will reject: the user clicks, waits, and gets an error for a condition that was knowable before the click. Not a correctness bug — the refusal holds — and not this ledger's to fix, but it will be hit on every manual test of MODEL-SERVE-006, so it is recorded rather than rediscovered.

NEW 2026-08-25 — THE UNPERSISTED DEPLOY ATOMS ARE THE SCHEDULER'S CONFIG. phase-4-deploy.tsx's comment names mpAutoRetrainAtom 'and friends' (per MODEL-FLOW-010-T08's field list: autoRetrain, warnSd, criticalSd, driftMonitor, driftThresholdPct) as surviving in the store with nothing persisting them, and declines to render them for exactly that reason. That was the right call and it is also a ready-made requirement: those five fields are what a schedule and a drift alarm need. MODEL-SERVE-006 should adopt them rather than invent a parallel set of names, and the wizard step can then render them honestly.

features.title: Audit — Replace Every UNVERIFIED Finding With a Fact
features.description: This ledger was written from another ledger, not from the tree. Nothing below MODEL-SERVE-000 should be scoped, estimated or started until these reads are done, because the shape of each downstream feature depends on what is already there. The precedent is direct: MODEL-FLOW-000's re-audit found five of seven tasks describing already-correct code and one whose premise was inverted, and the cost of that was a task list nobody could trust.

tasks.title: Read run_manifest.json's contents
tasks.detail: NARROWED 2026-08-24 by the MinIO observation — the object exists, is named run_manifest.json, and is 1.2 KiB, so this is no longer 'find out what the trainer uploads' but 'read one known 1.2 KiB file'. Download it and record its literal schema here. The three questions that decide downstream scope: (1) is there a checksum of model.joblib? (2) is the framework and its exact version recorded? (3) does it carry the featureSpecKey of the artifact it was fitted against, or must that be resolved through the run row? If (3) is yes, the three-hop chain collapses to two and MODEL-SERVE-000-T07 shrinks.

tasks.title: Establish whether Model has any notion of version
tasks.detail: packages/prisma/prisma/schema.prisma. MODEL-FLOW-010-T08 already caught this ledger's sibling asserting a row held fields it did not, so read the model, do not infer it from MODEL-FLOW-007's task titles. If Model is single-artifact with no version, MODEL-SERVE-001 is an additive entity; if it already versions, that feature shrinks to a stage column and a constraint.

tasks.title: Trace the preprocessing path end to end and decide how serving reuses it
tasks.detail_addendum: REVISED 2026-08-24: no longer 'trace the whole preprocessing path' — feature_columns is inlined in run_manifest.json, so column selection and order are already recoverable. Scope narrows to scalers alone. CHOOSE THE RUN DELIBERATELY: the observed OLS run has no scalers (target_scaled: false, and a 1.1 KiB model.joblib consistent with a bare estimator), so it cannot answer the question no matter how carefully it is read. Find a run whose dataset applied a scaler and start there.
tasks.detail: apps/python artifact_service.py (select_columns, force_keep_target, the scalers path) and feature_spec_service.py. Answer one question: can a serving process apply the identical transform to raw input by calling the same code, or does something in that path assume a whole parquet frame rather than a handful of rows? The answer decides whether serving is a thin loader or needs an extracted, shared transform module — a difference in kind, not degree. Do NOT plan to reimplement it either way; see the findings.

tasks.title: Determine which existing models are servable at all
tasks.detail: For the artifacts that exist, read feature_spec.json and check derived_from_target. Any model with a non-empty closure needs target history at inference and has a different request contract from one without. This is a fact-finding task, not a design one — but if it turns out MOST real soft-sensor models are in that set, /predict's shape changes and it is much cheaper to know now.

tasks.title: Decide the serving host
tasks.detail: Resolve decisions.serving_host_undecided. Read trainning-container.authorized.service.ts's watch() and confirm the reasoning in that decision against the actual code rather than against MODEL-FLOW-003-V01's incident note. Output is a chosen option with its reason, recorded in the decision — not a prototype.

tasks.title: Confirm the draft-prefix reclaim collision is real, then hand it upstream
tasks.detail: MODEL-FLOW-011 is unstarted, so this is a paper check against its T01/T02 details plus MODEL-FLOW-007-T10's. If confirmed, MODEL-FLOW-011-T05 (already drafted upstream) is the fix and it belongs in THAT ledger, not this one — this task's deliverable is the confirmation, not a guard.

tasks.title: Establish what retains the fitted artifact, and pin it if nothing does
tasks.detail:
OPENED 2026-08-24 from the observation that feature_spec.json is not in the run directory. Read DatasetArtifact's lifecycle: is there any path — a dataset edit, a version supersession, MODEL-FLOW-011's sweep, an admin delete — that can remove or orphan an artifact a ModelTrainingRun points at? Check the artifact's own retention alongside the draft-prefix question MODEL-SERVE-000-T06 asks; they are two objects with one consequence and it is cheaper to answer them in one read.

IF NOTHING RETAINS IT: the fix is upstream at Save Model, not here — MODEL-FLOW-007-T11 should record the artifact id and featureSpecKey on the saved Model so the reference is explicit and greppable, and whatever guards artifact deletion must treat a referencing ModelVersion the way MODEL-FLOW-011-T05 treats an adopted run. Deliverable of THIS task is the finding plus the upstream ticket, not a guard written in the wrong ledger.

DO NOT 'FIX' THIS BY COPYING feature_spec.json INTO THE RUN PREFIX. That trades a reference problem for a divergence problem and contradicts the adopt-by-pointer rule MODEL-FLOW-007-T10 states, for the same reason it states it.

acceptance_criteria: Every finding in this ledger marked UNVERIFIED is either confirmed with a file reference or corrected in place, with the correction stated rather than the original quietly edited.
manifest.json's contents are written down.
The serving host is chosen and the reason recorded.
It is known whether serving can call the existing preprocessing or must have it extracted.

verification.description: Re-read this ledger and confirm no UNVERIFIED marker remains. A finding that was checked and turned out WRONG must appear as a correction with both versions visible, the way MODEL-FLOW-010's findings record their reversals — silently deleting a wrong finding loses the evidence that the audit ran.

features.title: Model Version Registry — One Row Decides What Is In Production
features.description: Give a Model a versioned, staged history so that promotion and rollback are row changes. Nothing here serves anything; this is the pointer everything downstream reads.

tasks.title: ModelVersion entity
tasks.detail: Shape depends on MODEL-SERVE-000-T02. Fields: modelId, version, the artifact pointer and checksum, feature spec reference, framework + version, sourceRunId, sourceDatasetId, metrics, stage, timestamps, promotedById. A version row is IMMUTABLE except for stage — same discipline as MODEL-FLOW-007-T10's adopt-by-pointer: the row records what happened, it is not a workspace.
tasks.detail_addendum: REVISED 2026-08-24: the artifact reference is NOT optional and NOT derivable later. Because the run directory holds no feature spec (see findings), ModelVersion must record the fitted DatasetArtifact's id and its featureSpecKey explicitly, alongside the model object pointer. Resolving it at serve time by walking to the dataset's CURRENT artifact would be silently wrong for any model whose dataset was edited after training — and it would be wrong in the direction that still returns a number.

tasks.title: Stage machine and the single-production constraint
tasks.detail: STAGING -> PRODUCTION -> ARCHIVED. Enforce at most one PRODUCTION per modelId AT THE DATABASE, with a partial unique index, not in service code. Application-level uniqueness under concurrent promotes is the same class of hole MODEL-FLOW-007-T10's 409 guard closes for double-save, and the same reason MODEL-FLOW-002-T07 used a CHECK constraint rather than a service check.

tasks.title: Save Model creates version 1 in STAGING, never PRODUCTION
tasks.detail: Saving is not deploying. A wizard whose last click puts a model in front of live traffic has no step at which someone decides it should be. This is additive to MODEL-FLOW-007-T04's transaction, inside the same transaction — a Model with no version row is a state nothing downstream can interpret.

tasks.title: Promote and rollback endpoints
tasks.detail: POST .../versions/:v/promote and POST .../rollback, both recording who and when. Rollback is promote pointed at the previous PRODUCTION — not a distinct mechanism, so it cannot rot separately. Envelope per the findings.

tasks.title: Refuse to promote a version whose artifact cannot be loaded
tasks.detail: Verify object existence and checksum BEFORE flipping the stage. A promote that succeeds against a missing or altered object turns a deploy into an outage discovered by the first request, and the rollback path is then also untested. This is the one place a slow check is worth it.

tasks.title: Refuse to promote a version whose metrics fail a floor, unless overridden on the record
tasks.detail:
OPENED 2026-08-24 after observing r2 = -2.4068 on a run this project's own live verification recorded as successful. A negative R² is not a marginal model, it is a model with no predictive value, and there is currently no boundary at which anyone is asked whether it should go to production.

The floor must be a REFUSAL, not a warning. A warning at promote time is read once by the person who already decided to promote, which is the moment it has least effect. Make r2 <= 0 a hard block; anything above that is a judgement call and belongs to the human, not to a threshold this task invents.

An override must be possible — a deliberately weak model has legitimate uses (a baseline to beat, a smoke test of the serving path) — but it must be RECORDED on the ModelVersion with an actor and a reason, so that 'why is this in production' has an answer six months later. An override that leaves no trace is the same as no floor.

DO NOT PUT THIS IN THE WIZARD INSTEAD. Step 4 Evaluation showing a negative R² prominently is good and separate; MODEL-FLOW-004 owns it. The promote boundary needs its own gate because promotion is reachable without the wizard — see MODEL-SERVE-001-T04's endpoints.

tasks.title: Retain the trainer image digest a live version names
tasks.detail: OPENED 2026-08-24. run_manifest.json pins provenance by image_digest, which is the strongest form available — and worthless once that image leaves the registry. Establish whether the registry has any GC or tag-expiry policy, and if so, exclude digests named by a non-ARCHIVED ModelVersion. This is the same class of problem as MODEL-FLOW-011-T05 and MODEL-SERVE-000-T07: a reference held in one system to an object another system is free to delete. Third instance of the pattern in this project, which is the argument for stating it as a rule rather than fixing it three times.

acceptance_criteria: Save Model produces exactly one ModelVersion at STAGING and no PRODUCTION version.
Two concurrent promotes against one model cannot both leave a PRODUCTION row — enforced by the database, proven by a concurrent test rather than by reading the service.
Rollback restores the previous PRODUCTION version and is recorded with an actor.
Promoting a version whose object is missing or whose checksum does not match fails and leaves the current PRODUCTION untouched.
A ModelVersion row's artifact pointer, checksum and metrics are never updated after creation.

verification.description: Fire two promotes concurrently against different versions of one model and confirm exactly one PRODUCTION row survives. Sequential promotes would pass a weaker test while leaving the race entirely uncovered — the constraint this feature adds exists for the concurrent case.
Delete the object behind a STAGING version, attempt to promote it, and confirm both the refusal AND that the previously live version is still PRODUCTION and still loadable.
Complete Save Model and assert zero PRODUCTION rows exist for that model. The mirror of MODEL-FLOW-007-V01, one boundary later.

features.title: Serving Runtime and Synchronous /predict
features.description: A long-running process that loads PRODUCTION versions from object storage and answers bounded synchronous prediction requests. One image, many models.

tasks.title: Serving image, without the trainer's fit-time dependencies
tasks.detail: Note the deployment-currency trap MODEL-FLOW-000-T04's verification_note already recorded for the trainer: nothing in CI builds images/trainer/Dockerfile, so repo source being correct proves nothing about what is deployed. Do not inherit that. The serving image gets a CI build from the first commit, or it acquires the same untraceable drift.

tasks.title: Multi-model loader with a bounded cache
tasks.detail_addendum: REVISED 2026-08-24: verify model_sha256 (the field name is now known, not hypothesised) and verify image_digest against the serving runtime — noting that a digest match is not achievable if serving runs a DIFFERENT image from the trainer, which decisions.training_and_serving_are_separate_planes deliberately requires. So the digest is a provenance record to CHECK FOR PRESENCE and log, not a value to match. What must actually be validated at load is that the serving runtime's own library versions are compatible with the pickle; the digest tells you what to go and look up when they are not.
tasks.detail: Resolve model_id -> PRODUCTION version -> object; verify checksum; verify the recorded framework version against the runtime and REFUSE on a mismatch rather than warn (see findings — a silently-loaded mismatch produces plausible wrong numbers). Cache bounded by memory, not by entry count: models differ in size by orders of magnitude and a count-based cap sizes for the smallest one.

tasks.title: Warm the production set before reporting ready
tasks.detail: /healthz answers without touching MinIO or Postgres (a liveness probe that depends on them turns a dependency blip into a restart loop); /readyz answers only after the production set is loaded. Getting this backwards means traffic arrives during cold load and the first caller pays for everyone.

tasks.title: POST /predict, bounded and validated against feature_spec.json
tasks.detail: Validate presence, dtype and column ORDER against the spec, and cap rows per request. Reject with a message naming the offending column. sklearn's own error on a mismatched frame names a column and explains nothing — the same complaint MODEL-FLOW-010-T07 makes about pyarrow's 'No match for FieldRef.Name' reaching a user who cannot act on it. The range checks the dataset wizard's feature presets already express are the natural source for a range warning here; reuse rather than restate.

tasks.title: Apply the training-time preprocessing, by calling it
tasks.detail: Per MODEL-SERVE-000-T03's answer. If the path is callable, call it. If it is not, extract it into a module BOTH the trainer and the server import, and make the trainer use the extracted copy in the same change — leaving the trainer on the original and the server on a copy is precisely the drift this task exists to prevent, and it would pass every test written against either side alone.

tasks.title: Refuse target-derived models that are not given target history
tasks.detail: Read derived_from_target at LOAD time and fix the request contract from it, rather than discovering the gap per-request. Also validate the submitted history's sampling interval against the spec. A model in this class served without history does not error — it predicts from imputed or absent lags and returns a number, which is the failure mode with no symptom.

tasks.title: Invalidate the cache on promote
tasks.detail: After a promote, replicas holding the old version keep serving it until something tells them. Whatever the mechanism (a short TTL on the version lookup is the cheapest and is probably enough), the CONTRACT is what matters: state the maximum time a promoted version can take to become live, and make it a number someone chose rather than an emergent property. Silent divergence between two replicas answering the same request differently is very hard to diagnose from the outside.

acceptance_criteria: A promoted model answers /predict with no image rebuild and no redeploy.
A request missing a required column is refused with that column named — not a 500 from the estimator.
A model whose feature spec is target-derived cannot be served without target history, and the refusal states why.
The transform applied at inference is the SAME CODE as the one applied at training, not an equivalent one.
A checksum or framework-version mismatch prevents a load; it never degrades to a warning.
/healthz does not depend on MinIO or Postgres; /readyz does.
After a promote, every replica serves the new version within the stated bound.

verification.description: PROVE NO SKEW, WHICH IS THE WHOLE POINT: take a row from the model's own test split, send it through /predict, and assert the prediction matches the value in that run's predictions artifact to numerical tolerance. Any test using synthetic input proves the endpoint returns a float, which is not the claim. This is the V02-of-MODEL-FLOW-000 of this ledger — the one verification whose absence would make everything else look fine.

Promote a new version while /predict is under continuous load and confirm every response is answerable by SOME valid version, with the switchover inside the stated bound and no request failing at the boundary.

Load a model whose feature spec declares a non-empty derived_from_target and confirm a history-less request is refused. Then submit history at the WRONG sampling interval and confirm it is also refused — a serving process that accepts the second has not implemented this task, only half of it.
Point the loader at an object whose bytes have been altered and confirm the load fails on checksum rather than succeeding.

features.title: Batch Prediction and Job Results
features.description: Score a parquet input in object storage as an asynchronous job, and return the result by reference. This is the '/predict + /result' pair from the original question, split because they are two different operations.

tasks.title: PredictionJob entity and its state machine
tasks.detail: QUEUED/RUNNING/SUCCEEDED/FAILED/CANCELED, mirroring ModelTrainingRun's vocabulary rather than inventing a parallel one. State in Postgres, never in process memory — MODEL-FLOW-003-V01's stranded run is the demonstration of what in-memory job tracking does across a restart, and a result endpoint answering 404 for a job that finished is the same bug with a friendlier face.

tasks.title: POST /predict:batch with an idempotency key
tasks.detail: Returns a job id immediately. The idempotency key is not optional: MODEL-FLOW-003-T09 had to add poll-failure tolerance specifically because a transient error pushed users toward a retry that would spawn a SECOND container against the same draft. A batch endpoint without a key has the identical hole and the same trigger.

tasks.title: Batch worker, chunked
tasks.detail: Stream the input rather than loading it whole. MODEL-FLOW-010-V03 exists because a single unbounded read at 8,000 tags produced 76MB where 489KB was needed; a batch scorer is the most likely place for that to reappear, and it will reappear on someone else's data, not in a test.

tasks.title: GET /jobs/:id — status, and the output by presigned reference
tasks.detail: Never stream result bytes through the API. Reuse the existing presign path (artifact_service.presign_artifact) rather than writing a second one, and honour MODEL-FLOW-000-T06's rule: neither the presign request nor the URL reaches a log, because the URL IS the capability.

tasks.title: Record which version scored the batch
tasks.detail: Pin the version at job START and store it on the job. A long batch spanning a promote must not silently score its first half on one model and its second on another — and a result whose model is 'whatever was production at some point' cannot be reproduced or defended later.

acceptance_criteria: The batch endpoint returns a job id without waiting for the work.
Job state survives a restart of the process that created it.
Results are delivered by presigned reference; no result bytes traverse the API.
The same idempotency key cannot produce two jobs.
Every job records the exact model version that scored it, pinned at start.
A batch over a wide input keeps memory bounded — no unbounded read of the input frame.

verification.description: Submit a batch, restart the serving process mid-flight, and confirm GET /jobs/:id still reports truthfully — either a completed job or a job that reached a terminal FAILED with a stated reason. Permanently RUNNING is the failure this checks for, and it is the exact state MODEL-FLOW-003-V01 observed on the training side.
Submit the same idempotency key twice concurrently and confirm one job. Sequential submission is a weaker test that a naive check would also pass.

Promote a new version DURING a running batch and confirm the output was scored end to end by the pinned version, asserted from the job row and the output's own recorded version — not inferred from timing.

features.title: POST /retrain — Trigger Only
features.blocked_on: The same decision MODEL-FLOW-005 is blocked on — see MODEL-FLOW decisions.fine_tuning_undefined and this ledger's decisions.retrain_and_fine_tuning_are_one_question. Until 'retrain' is defined (a fresh fit on a widened window? a hyperparameter search reusing the split? a warm start on a framework that supports one?), the tasks below describe a job whose work is unspecified. Note this blocker is shared, not duplicated: resolving it unblocks both features at once and must not be counted twice.
features.description: An endpoint that records the intent to retrain and returns. The work is done by the existing trainer image, spawned the way MODEL-FLOW-003-T04 already spawns it. A successful retrain produces a new ModelVersion at STAGING and promotes nothing.

tasks.title: Define what retrain means, and write it in the shared decision
tasks.detail: This is the whole blocker and it is a product decision, not an engineering one. Everything below is unscopeable until it lands. Write the answer into MODEL-FLOW decisions.fine_tuning_undefined so both ledgers read one definition.

tasks.title: Trigger endpoint with idempotency and a per-model lock
tasks.detail: Three clicks must not become three containers competing for the same 8 GiB. MODEL-FLOW-000-T03 established that /scratch's tmpfs shares the container's memory cgroup, so concurrent fits are not merely slow, they are a plausible OOM.

tasks.title: Spawn the existing trainer; never fit in the serving process
tasks.detail: Per decisions.training_and_serving_are_separate_planes.

tasks.title: On success, create a STAGING version — promote nothing
tasks.detail: Auto-promotion would put an unreviewed model in front of live traffic on a schedule, which is a decision no one made. MODEL-SERVE-001-T03 takes the same position for Save Model, for the same reason.

tasks.title: Compare the candidate against the incumbent, and publish the comparison
tasks.detail: The comparison is only meaningful on a common evaluation basis; a retrain on a widened window has a different test split, so a raw R² delta is not a like-for-like number. State the basis alongside the numbers rather than presenting a delta that reads as one and is not — the same discipline MODEL-FLOW-010-T06 applies to publishing the holdout's missing rate beside every metric.

acceptance_criteria: The endpoint returns immediately with a job id and never fits in-process.
Concurrent triggers for one model produce one job.
A successful retrain creates a STAGING version and changes no PRODUCTION pointer.
The candidate-versus-incumbent comparison states its evaluation basis, and refuses to present a delta across incomparable bases as if it were one.

verification.description: Trigger a retrain and confirm PRODUCTION is unchanged after it succeeds. The point of the feature is what it does NOT do.
Fire three concurrent triggers and confirm one container. Count containers, not jobs — a service that dedupes the row but spawns three is the failure this guards.

features.title: Prediction Logging and Drift Signal
features.description: Record inputs and predictions so that a model going wrong is observable, and so that a future automatic retrain has a trigger that is a measurement rather than a calendar.

tasks.title: Log request features, prediction and version to the time-series store
tasks.detail: Sampled, not every request — full-fidelity logging of a high-rate soft sensor is a second data pipeline nobody planned for. State the sampling rate; a rate chosen by accident makes every downstream statistic uninterpretable.

tasks.title: Compare live input distributions against the training distribution
tasks.detail: The training distribution is already characterised — column_stats is the sidecar the dataset wizard writes and MODEL-FLOW-010-T04 reads. Compare against it rather than recomputing a baseline, so both surfaces agree on what 'normal' was.

tasks.title: Join late-arriving ground truth and track live error
tasks.detail: For a lab-sampled target the truth arrives hours or days later, so this is a delayed join, not a live metric. Publish the missing/Bad rate of the joined window beside the error, for the reason MODEL-FLOW-010-T06 gives: with no imputation, a hole depresses the score with no trace of why.

features.scope_correction: REVISED 2026-08-25. This feature was written assuming prediction logging is a sampled by-product of synchronous requests. With MODEL-SERVE-006, the primary prediction stream is the hourly window record, which is complete rather than sampled and already carries version and missing rate. So T01's sampling concern applies to MODEL-SERVE-002's sync path only, and T02 (drift vs column_stats) and T03 (late ground-truth join) now read from InferenceWindow. They stay here rather than moving into 006 because they are analysis over the record, not production of it.
features.acceptance_criteria_correction: The first two criteria listed here ('r2 at or below zero cannot be promoted' and 'the image digest is retained') were misfiled — they belong to MODEL-SERVE-001-T06 and -T07 respectively and are removed from this feature. Recorded rather than silently deleted, per MODEL-SERVE-000-V01's rule.
acceptance_criteria: A version whose r2 is at or below zero cannot be promoted without an override recorded with an actor and a reason.
The trainer image digest a live version names is retained for as long as that version is not ARCHIVED.
Predictions are logged with their model version and the logging is sampled at a stated, deliberate rate.
Drift is measured against the artifact's own column_stats, not a separately-computed baseline.
Live error is reported only for windows where ground truth has actually arrived, with the joined window's missing rate published beside it.

verification.description: Feed input shifted well outside the training distribution and confirm the drift signal fires. Feeding in-distribution data proves only that nothing crashed.

features.title: Scheduled Hourly Inference — Windows, Logs, and the Monitoring Record
features.description: Run a promoted model on a fixed cadence, writing one predictions parquet and one metrics document per time window, with per-run logs readable afterwards. This is the feature that makes 'deployed' mean something. It needs no serving process — see decisions.short_lived_containers_for_scheduled_inference.

dependency_notes.MODEL-FLOW-004: HARD, not conventional. Step 4 currently computes its own metrics client-side (see findings), so until it reads the run's real metrics there is no surface on which a metric registry or a monitoring series means anything. Building the schedule first would produce a correct monitoring record beside a screen showing unrelated numbers.
dependency_notes.MODEL-FLOW-011: Specifically T04, orphaned-RUNNING reconciliation. MODEL-FLOW-003-V01 observed ONE stranded RUNNING row from ONE nest restart. At 24 windows a day that stops being an incident and becomes a background rate, and every stranded row is a permanent hole in the monitoring record. Reconciliation must exist before the cadence does, not after.
dependency_notes.MODEL-SERVE-002: NOT a dependency, deliberately. Synchronous /predict is a different requirement; this feature must not wait on it and must not build a serving process to get a scheduled run.

findings: THE UNIT IS A TIME WINDOW, NOT A TICK. A scheduler written as 'every hour, read the latest values, predict' loses data permanently on every miss, cannot say which hours are missing, and has no backfill path. A scheduler written as 'ensure a row exists for every window' gets gap detection, backfill and idempotency from one UNIQUE constraint. This is the single decision the whole feature rests on.

SCHEDULED WORK HAS NO CALLER, WHICH CHANGES WHAT FAILURE MEANS. A sync request that fails returns an error to someone who is waiting. A window that fails is observed by nobody. So the feature is not complete when windows succeed — it is complete when a window that DOESN'T run is visible. Hence T10, which is the one task here that must not be cut.

setInterval().unref() IS ADEQUATE HERE, BUT FOR A DIFFERENT REASON THAN IT WAS ADEQUATE FOR THE SWEEPER. MODEL-FLOW-011-T03 chose it because a missed sweep costs nothing — next tick does the work. A missed inference window is a permanent gap. It is still adequate, but ONLY because the tick's job is an idempotent insert keyed on window_start, so a later tick recovers what an earlier one missed. If the tick ever predicts directly, this mechanism becomes wrong.

PI TAGS DO NOT ARRIVE TOGETHER AND THE LAB TARGET ARRIVES MUCH LATER. window_end = now() yields a frame that is structurally complete and factually empty in places — and the model will score it without error, because the columns exist. This is the same mechanism MODEL-FLOW-010-T06 records for the holdout (no imputation, so a hole reaches predict() and depresses the result with no trace), except it recurs every hour instead of once. Hence a deliberate lag (T04) and a per-window missing rate (T05).

A PROMOTE MID-SERIES IS INDISTINGUISHABLE FROM A PROCESS CHANGE UNLESS THE VERSION IS PINNED PER WINDOW. Two adjacent points from different model versions render as a step change on the same axis as a real process shift, and someone will spend days on the wrong hypothesis. Pinning also yields shadow evaluation for free: two rows, same window, different versions.

tasks.title: InferenceWindow entity, keyed on (modelVersionId, windowStart)
tasks.detail:
Fields: modelId, modelVersionId, windowStart, windowEnd, status (PENDING|RUNNING|SUCCEEDED|FAILED|SKIPPED), predictionsKey, metricsKey, inputRows, missingPct, imageDigest, runId, startedAt, finishedAt, failureReason.

UNIQUE (modelVersionId, windowStart) IS THE WHOLE DESIGN. It is the idempotency mechanism, so this feature needs no idempotency key of the kind MODEL-SERVE-003-T02 requires — windowStart is the natural key and a repeated insert is a no-op. It also makes gaps queryable (status != 'SUCCEEDED') and makes backfill an insert rather than a code path.

SKIPPED is a real terminal status, not a synonym for FAILED: a window with too few input rows to score was correctly not attempted, and conflating it with a failure would make the staleness alarm cry wolf on a quiet plant.

tasks.title: The tick inserts windows and nothing else
tasks.detail:
setInterval(...).unref() in onModuleInit, matching MODEL-FLOW-011-T03's mechanism and PreprocessingJobService.scheduleStragglerSweep's precedent. Env-configurable, <= 0 disables.

The tick does exactly two things: insert PENDING rows for windows that have none, and reconcile rows stuck in RUNNING past a timeout. IT MUST NOT SCORE ANYTHING. Scoring in the tick reintroduces every property this design exists to avoid — a missed tick becomes a lost window, the interval becomes load-bearing, and a slow run delays the next one. Errors logged and swallowed; anything the tick missed is still eligible next time, which is only true because of T01's key.

tasks.title: infer.py as a second entrypoint on the existing trainer image
tasks.detail:
Reads its window spec from a /claim-style callback exactly as train.py does, resolves the model object and scaler state (MODEL-SERVE-000-T03 must have answered where scalers live — this task is blocked in practice until it has), scores, writes predictions.parquet and metrics.json, reports through /log and /complete.

Same image as the trainer so both entrypoints unpickle with the same library versions, and so image_digest provenance works identically. HEED MODEL-FLOW-000-T04's warning: nothing in CI builds images/trainer/Dockerfile, so a correct repo and a stale deployed image are indistinguishable today. Adding an entrypoint makes that worse, because a deployed image without infer.py fails in a way that looks like a scheduler bug. Add the CI build in this task, not later.

tasks.title: Window boundaries from a chosen ingestion lag
tasks.detail:
windowEnd = now() - lag, where lag is a configured value someone decided, per model. Do NOT default it to zero and do not derive it from the cadence — freshness and completeness genuinely trade against each other here and the trade must be made deliberately.

Measure before choosing: the 8 tags in the observed run's feature_columns (AI001A2.PV, AI206.PV, TI202/203/205/206/207.PV, Spgr_in_feed_Header_1) against RYGPDH01, worst-case arrival. The lab target's own latency is a different and much longer number and belongs to T08, not here — inference needs features only.

tasks.title: Record inputRows and missingPct per window
tasks.detail: On the row, not only inside the output object, so a series query can join them without opening parquet. Without this, a prediction series that starts wandering is indistinguishable between real process drift and a sensor that stopped reporting — and the second is far more common. Same rule and same reason as MODEL-FLOW-010-T06's insistence that the holdout's missing rate be published beside every figure.

tasks.title: Partitioned output layout for the monitoring record
tasks.detail:
inference/{modelId}/{modelVersionId}/dt=YYYY-MM-DD/hour=HH/predictions.parquet, plus metrics.json alongside. Hive-style so a date range reads without listing everything.

KEPT SEPARATE FROM drafts/{draftId}/runs/{runId}/predictions.parquet ON PURPOSE: that object is the test-split prediction, immutable and backward-looking; this one is an append-only operational record with different retention and a different access pattern. Also a different root from drafts/, which the findings note is already shared by two entities.

Do not couple the read path to one-file-per-hour. 8,760 objects per model-year is fine for MinIO and slow to scan; daily compaction is not needed on day one but becomes needed, and a reader that assumes hourly files has to be rewritten then.

tasks.title: Pin modelVersionId at window creation, and expose version boundaries
tasks.detail: Already in T01's key; this task is the read side. Any series rendering must be able to say where a version changed, because the alternative is a step change attributed to the process. Falls out for free: two rows for one windowStart under different versions is a shadow comparison, which is the safe way to exercise a candidate — including the current r2 = -2.4068 model — without promoting it.

tasks.title: Metric registry — derived from predictions, recomputable, selectable from the UI
tasks.detail:
Per decisions.metrics_are_derived_from_predictions_not_computed_at_fit. One definition set, applied to test-split predictions for evaluation and to window predictions for monitoring, so the two are the same number computed the same way.

Each registry entry declares whether it is BACKFILLABLE from (actual, predicted) plus run_manifest scalars, or requires inputs not retained. That flag is not documentation — it is what stops a comparison table silently mixing metrics that exist for all history with metrics that exist only for new runs.

mpSelectedMetricsAtom becomes a real selection over this registry instead of a filter over browser-computed values. THAT SUBSTITUTION IS ONLY MEANINGFUL AFTER MODEL-FLOW-004 (see findings): applied to today's phase-3-evaluation.tsx it would change which locally-computed numbers are displayed and nothing else.

tasks.title: Persist the schedule, and adopt the existing deploy atoms rather than new ones
tasks.detail:
Per-model schedule config: enabled, cadence, lag (T04), and the five fields phase-4-deploy.tsx already holds unpersisted in the store — autoRetrain, warnSd, criticalSd, driftMonitor, driftThresholdPct (per MODEL-FLOW-010-T08's field list). USE THOSE NAMES. A parallel set means the wizard and the scheduler describe the same setting in two vocabularies, and reconciling them later is worse than adopting them now.

This is the change that lets phase-4-deploy.tsx render those controls honestly, which its own comment declines to do today for the stated reason that nothing persists them.

tasks.title: Staleness alarm on the absence of successful windows
tasks.detail:
If no window has reached SUCCEEDED for longer than a configured multiple of the cadence, raise it. DO NOT CUT THIS TASK. Every other task in this feature makes the monitoring record trustworthy; this is the only one that reveals when the record has stopped being written. A drift dashboard with no incoming data looks calm, and calm is exactly the wrong signal.

SKIPPED windows must not silence the alarm and must not trigger it either — they are a legitimate quiet plant, and treating them as either extreme makes the alarm useless in one direction or the other.

tasks.title: Backfill by inserting windows, with no separate code path
tasks.detail: A range request inserts PENDING rows for windows that have none. The worker cannot distinguish backfill from live, which is the point — a second code path is a second set of bugs, and it would be exercised only during incidents. T01's UNIQUE constraint means over-requesting a range is harmless.

tasks.title: Derive deployStatus from the last successful window
tasks.detail:
Per decisions.deploy_status_currently_asserts_something_untrue. Today `updateModel(modelId, { deployStatus: 'running' })` writes a claim nothing backs. Once windows exist, that claim has a real referent and must be READ from it, not written beside it. Leaving both means two sources of truth for 'is this deployed', and the stale one wins whenever someone forgets to update it.

Phase-4-deploy.tsx's own structure survives this change unharmed: deploy stays a second write after save, and a failed deploy still leaves a saved model. What changes is that the second write enables a schedule instead of setting a string.

acceptance_criteria: A promoted model produces one predictions object and one metrics document per window, on the configured cadence, with no manual action.
Every window is queryable by its own boundaries, and windows that did not succeed are listable as gaps.
A missed or failed window can be backfilled by requesting its range, through the same worker that runs live windows.
Requesting an already-present window is a no-op — enforced by a unique constraint, not by a service check.
Each window records the model version that scored it, pinned at creation, and a series can show where the version changed.
Each window records its input row count and missing rate on the row itself.
Window boundaries respect a configured ingestion lag; the lag is a chosen value, not a default of zero.
Per-window logs are readable after the container exits, through the same path training logs already use.
The absence of successful windows raises an alarm; SKIPPED windows neither raise nor suppress it.
Evaluation and monitoring metrics come from one registry applied to stored predictions, and each entry states whether it is backfillable.
Adding a metric to the registry requires no retraining and no refit to populate it for past runs — for backfillable entries.
deployStatus is derived from the last successful window; no caller sets it directly.
The schedule reuses the field names the wizard's existing deploy atoms already use.

verification.description: THE ONLY TEST THAT DISTINGUISHES A WORKING SCHEDULER FROM ONE THAT HAS NOT YET MISSED: stop the scheduler for three cadence periods, restart it, and confirm all three absent windows are (a) visible as gaps, (b) backfillable, and (c) that backfilling them produces output indistinguishable from live windows. A test that only asserts normal windows succeed cannot tell these apart.

Kill the backend mid-window, restart, and confirm the row reaches a terminal status rather than staying RUNNING. This is MODEL-FLOW-003-V01's observed orphan, reproduced deliberately at a cadence where it will recur. If MODEL-FLOW-011-T04 has not landed, this verification fails by design and is the evidence that the dependency is real.

Run a window against data with a KNOWN hole in one feature tag, and confirm both that missingPct records it and that the prediction is not silently produced as if the frame were complete. Running against clean data proves only that the happy path works, which is not what T05 exists for.
Promote a new version between two windows and confirm the series exposes the boundary — asserted from the pinned modelVersionId on each row, not inferred from timestamps.

Add a backfillable metric to the registry and confirm it populates for a run that predates the addition, with NO retraining. Then attempt the same with an entry marked not-backfillable and confirm it is reported as unavailable for that run rather than computed from something it should not use.

Enable a schedule, let one window succeed, then disable the model's schedule and confirm deployStatus changes with the record rather than remaining whatever was last written. A status that can only be set forward is the bug this checks for.

Insert two windows for one windowStart under two different versions and confirm both score and store independently — the shadow-evaluation path T07 claims comes for free, verified rather than assumed.

global_definition_of_done: A scheduled model produces one record per time window; a window that did not run is visible as a gap and backfillable through the same path a live window uses.
Evaluation and monitoring read one metric registry over stored predictions — adding a backfillable metric never requires a refit.
'Deployed' is derived from the monitoring record, never asserted by a caller.

A production model's fitted artifact and feature spec are retained and pinned for as long as any version references them — the model object and the spec it needs are two objects in different places, and losing either is the same outage.
A saved Model can be promoted to production and rolled back without building or deploying an image.
At most one PRODUCTION version exists per model, enforced by the database.
The transform applied at inference is the same code as the one applied at training — proven by scoring a training-set row through the live endpoint, not by inspection.
A model that cannot be served correctly (target-derived features without history, framework mismatch, bad checksum) is refused at load or at request, never served with a plausible wrong answer.
Batch results are delivered by reference; no result bytes and no presigned URLs pass through a log.
Job state survives a process restart.
Retrain produces a candidate; a human promotes it.
No feature in this ledger writes to any MODEL-FLOW wizard path, and no MODEL-FLOW feature is reopened to accommodate one.
